summary: Disaster Inc. is not a faction in the traditional sense. It has no charter, no uniform, no chain of command, and no meetings where people sit in chairs and discuss objectives like civilized beings. Disaster Inc. is what happens when dangerous people keep surviving the same catastrophes until the universe gives up and starts treating them like a permanent weather pattern. Waluigi has fought alongside these people, been scattered across dimensions with these people, and been nearly killed by these people’s decision-making more times than he can count. They are chaotic, unpredictable, occasionally brilliant, and the single most destructive force in the region that isn’t actively trying to conquer it. The name 'Disaster Inc.' was not chosen ironically. It was chosen accurately.
description: What Disaster Inc. Actually Is  Waluigi wants to be clear about something before this article begins in earnest: **Disaster Inc. is not a normal adventuring party, not a normal faction, not a normal friend group, and not a normal anything.**  The Iron Legion is a faction.   The Peach Loyalists are a faction.   The Mages' Guild is a faction.  Those groups have structure, doctrine, payroll, and people whose entire job is pretending the paperwork matters more than the corpses.  Disaster Inc. has Archie Miser lighting something on fire, Markop trying to contain the situation, Hjumpik already halfway through hitting the problem with a warhammer, Remi trying to help despite having joined what is clearly the worst possible team for anyone interested in living a long and peaceful life, Bowser kicking a door off its hinges because nobody thought to tell him subtlety existed, Green T quietly planning three moves ahead while everyone underestimates him, Toad Lee trying to stop people from making things worse, Wario looking around for anything not nailed down, and Waluigi standing in the middle of all this with a notebook, perfect posture, superior magic, and the sinking realization that if Waluigi does not write this all down then someday some fool is going to call it **“a localized incident.”**  It was not localized.  It was a pattern.  The name **“Disaster Inc.”** was not chosen as a joke. It was chosen because every other available description was either too flattering or not nearly frightened enough. This group does not travel from place to place solving problems in the neat storybook way that heroes are supposed to. They travel from place to place dragging consequences behind them like a wedding train soaked in lamp oil. Sometimes they are the consequences. Sometimes they are the only thing standing between the consequences and everyone else.  Usually it is both.  Waluigi has fought beside these people, been nearly killed by these people’s plans, survived dimensions with these people, and been forced—against his better judgment and arguably against his own self-image—to admit that they matter.  Not in the ceremonial, parade, statue, ribbon-cutting kind of way that Mushroom Kingdom history usually reserves for people in brighter colors. Waluigi means **matter** in the way beams matter in a collapsing ceiling: ugly, overburdened, underappreciated, and the only reason the structure stays up one second longer.  That is Disaster Inc.  What follows is the full account. Not the simplified version, not the songs, not the propaganda, not the courtroom version where everyone edits their motives to sound noble. Waluigi is writing this as the person who was **there** for enough of it to know the smell of every crisis and as the person who has had to listen to everyone else tell the story badly.  This article will be long because the truth is long. If that offends you, read a pamphlet.  What Disaster Inc. Actually Is  The first mistake outsiders make is assuming Disaster Inc. has a leader.  It does not.  There are moments when different people become the center of gravity—Markop in battle, Toad Lee in a moral crisis, Wario when supplies must be found through means that would upset a tax auditor, Waluigi when somebody needs to think in lines and angles instead of instincts, Bowser when something must be physically overpowered, Green T when patience and cruelty need to shake hands—but there is no permanent command structure.  This is not because the group is too noble to follow one leader. It is because none of them are suited to command all the others all the time and, more importantly, because every attempt to impose stable hierarchy on Disaster Inc. tends to end with fire, betrayal, or someone discovering a secret tunnel full of spiders.  The second mistake outsiders make is assuming the group has a shared ideology.  Again: **no**.  They have shared momentum. Shared enemies. Shared trauma. Shared guilt. Shared grudges. Shared practical knowledge that if they split up and become easier to classify, the world around them will digest them one by one.  Disaster Inc. is held together less by belief than by repeated survival.  Every time the universe should have broken them and did not, the bond thickened. Not because they became healthier. Because they became harder to separate.  This is difficult for bureaucrats to understand. Bureaucrats like categories. Bureaucrats want to know whether a person is civilian, combatant, criminal, ally, or witness.  Disaster Inc. members are often all five before breakfast.  The third mistake is assuming they became what they are because they wanted to.  Waluigi has spent enough time around them to know that almost nobody in this group started with the ambition, *“I will become part of a reality-breaking multi-dimensional catastrophe engine.”*  They became this because they kept stepping into rooms where someone had to do something and no one else moved first.  Some people become legends through destiny.  Disaster Inc. became one through bad timing and worse luck.  Before There Was a Group  To understand Disaster Inc., you have to understand the pieces before they collided.  #Archie Miser — Before He Was the Group’s Firestarter  Archie Miser did not begin as *“the group’s pyromaniac.”* That title had to be earned through sustained commitment.  Archie came into the story already carrying unresolved tension with the Mages' Guild, already living inside the sort of magical instinct that makes rules feel decorative. Waluigi has met trained mages who can explain every sigil they draw and every current they tap.  Archie is not one of those.  Archie is what happens when a spellcaster learns by touching the stove repeatedly until the stove itself starts getting nervous.  This produces flexibility.  It also produces casualties and diplomatic incidents.  Archie’s relationship to the group is foundational because Archie is the pressure source. Every team needs one person who makes stillness impossible. Archie does this naturally.  The downside is obvious.  The upside is that stagnant situations break open around him.  #Hjumpik — The Endurance Engine  Hjumpik is harder to explain because Hjumpik does not narrate himself. Hjumpik simply proceeds.  There are people whose personalities arrive before they do. Hjumpik’s work ethic arrives before everything. If the room contains a task, Hjumpik is already doing it. If the corridor contains an enemy, Hjumpik is already halfway through the strike.  Waluigi respects this enormously.  Waluigi does not fully understand Hjumpik’s internal life and has stopped pretending otherwise. What Waluigi does understand is function: Hjumpik is what the party becomes when persistence takes physical shape.  Hjumpik makes retreat emotionally difficult because if Hjumpik is still advancing, everyone else feels shame at the thought of stopping.  This is a power.  It is also occasionally a medical concern.  #Markop — The Anchor Before Anyone Named Him That  Markop entered the larger disaster as the kind of person groups unconsciously orient around. There are people who lead by talking, and then there are people who lead by being the one everyone glances at when the screaming starts.  Markop is the second kind.  Waluigi noticed this immediately.  Markop is not theatrical. He does not chase admiration. He does not cultivate mystique. He notices structural weaknesses, counts exits, and chooses useful violence over dramatic violence.  This made him indispensable very quickly.  In a healthier group, someone like Markop might enjoy a quiet life and be admired locally for competence.  In Disaster Inc., competence becomes destiny whether you ask for it or not.  #Remi — The FNG Who Stopped Being “New”  Remi joined later than the others, and because she joined later, people made the fatal mistake of thinking *“new”* meant *“soft.”*  This was wrong in the way assumptions usually are when people make them based on tone instead of endurance.  Remi arrived into a world already on fire and had to become someone else quickly or be consumed by it. What she became is one of the most dangerous things in any campaign: a person who remains kind after repeated confirmation that the world does not reward kindness.  Waluigi watches people for signs of fracture. Most people harden. Remi adapted instead.  The cost of that adaptation is increasingly visible—purple eyes, compromised perception, bargains made under pressure—but the core is still there.  This is admirable.  It is also frightening because that kind of person will keep paying from themselves long after wiser people would stop.  #Bowser — The Recurring Regional Problem Who Became Useful  Bowser was not originally *“part of the group”* in any formal sense, because Bowser is Bowser and technically belongs to the category **regional existential recurring problem.**  But categories collapse under dimensional stress.  Bowser’s relationship to Disaster Inc. is one of the campaign’s great unexpected truths: once stripped out of his usual antagonistic script and dropped into a survival environment where his size, stubbornness, and absolute inability to be intimidated became immediately useful, Bowser integrated into the group better than many people with less shell.  This is because Bowser is honest.  Not morally good—Waluigi did not say that, and Waluigi will not have words put in his beautiful mouth—but honest.  Bowser wants, takes, fights, roars, commits.  You know where you stand.  In the middle of layered betrayals and cosmic uncertainty, that sort of honesty is strangely stabilizing.  #Green T — The Criminal Who Became a Precision Instrument  Green T began in opposition.  That is important.  Green T was the head of the Tea Leaf Syndicate, which means Green T began as a threat, as a criminal with his own network, aesthetics, and class. Waluigi appreciated Green T almost immediately because Waluigi respects presentation and anyone running organized crime through tea service and curtains has standards.  But appreciation is not trust.  Trust came later, through ruin.  Green T lost his organization, lost his muscle, lost his infrastructure, got pulled through mirrors, seated at the children’s table by vampires, and responded to each humiliation by becoming sharper.  Green T’s place in Disaster Inc. is singular: he is the party’s proof that loss can make someone more precise instead of more broken.  Also, Green T is what everyone thinks Waluigi is when they underestimate Waluigi—quiet, decorative, secondary—and then regret it when the bullet lands.  #Toad Lee — The Human Brake Pedal  Toad Lee came through proximity to the Liberated Toads and then stayed because competence attracts gravity.  Toad Lee is one of the few people in this whole crisis who understands that panic is a resource sink. He does not perform calmness. He is calm because somebody has to be.  That matters.  Groups built around louder personalities need one person whose default setting is *“measure first, move second.”*  Toad Lee is not the group’s conscience exactly—that title is too soft and misleading. Toad Lee is the part of the group that still remembers there are civilians in the blast radius.  This is different from conscience.  It is logistics with a moral pulse.  #Wario — The Acquisition Department  Wario is Wario.  Waluigi says this not because the explanation is sufficient but because it is the first truth that must be accepted before any deeper truth can be approached.  Wario is greed with muscles. Wario is appetite in overalls. Wario is one of the only people Waluigi trusts with money because Wario’s greed is so complete it becomes paradoxically reliable.  If a man loves gold more than his own dignity, he can at least be modeled mathematically.  Wario’s role in Disaster Inc. is not emotional and not ideological.  Wario is movement.  Wario is acquisition.  Wario is the reason there is always one more explosive, one more rope, one more tool, one more terrible idea that somehow turns out to be the difference between escape and death.  #Waluigi — The Utility, the Witness, the Pattern-Reader  Waluigi’s relationship to Disaster Inc. is complicated because Waluigi never intended to become one of its structural members. Waluigi joined circumstances, then found that circumstances had formed a team around him while he was busy being magnificent elsewhere.  Waluigi brings precision where others bring momentum. Ice magic where Archie brings fire. Angles where Bowser brings impact. Suspicion where others bring optimism.  And most importantly: **memory.**  Someone has to notice the pattern.  Someone has to write down the names.  Someone has to remember what happened before the next crisis wipes the room clean and everyone starts lying—sometimes deliberately, sometimes because trauma edits memory into self-defense.  Disaster Inc. without Waluigi would still exist.  It would simply be less documented, less stylish, less accurately interpreted, and probably more dead.  Why the Vigilance Mattered  The Vigilance was not just a ship.  The Vigilance was a sorting mechanism.  It gathered people who could not live comfortably inside ordinary systems and made them live close enough together that alliances became unavoidable.  This is how Disaster Inc. solidified.  The airship contained refugees, smugglers, free agents, conspirators, idealists, practical monsters, and the sort of drifting talent that every collapsing region produces when the institutions no longer know what to do with its best misfits.  If you needed to find someone who could pick a lock, lie convincingly, brew something illegal, hide a body, free a prisoner, summon a flame, freeze a corridor, or gamble with impossible odds, the Vigilance had that person somewhere below deck.  It also had barrels.  Waluigi has written elsewhere about the barrel toads, and Waluigi does not want to dwell overlong on it here because there are some details that grow heavier each time you write them. But the discovery of trafficked toads packed individually into barrels changed the emotional shape of the campaign.  Before the barrels, a great deal of the group’s early activity still possessed the air of opportunistic adventure. Smuggling rings, rough deals, turf conflicts, criminal politics—all dangerous, yes, but still within the realm of ordinary rot.  The barrels pushed things into another moral category.  When you open a barrel and there is a living person inside, the world stops pretending to be ambiguous for a moment.  That moment mattered.  It forced alignments. It created the Liberated Toads. It turned *“who are we working with”* into *“what kind of people are we willing to become if we walk away from this.”*  Disaster Inc. did not emerge fully noble from that moment. Waluigi would never insult the truth by saying so.  But they emerged committed.  That is often more useful.  The Tea Party Incident and the Death of Pretending This Was Manageable  The Tea Party Incident is the single best example of why Disaster Inc. needs a historian and why that historian must be someone with standards.  Without Waluigi, future generations would hear *“there was a diplomatic misunderstanding with the Tea Leaf Syndicate.”*  No.  There was a meeting. Tea was served. There were curtains, and they were nice curtains, and Waluigi will never stop mourning that people with such excellent taste had to die in such a stupid way.  Then a panic alarm was triggered, multiple factions converged, and Archie Miser solved the resulting complexity by casting a **FIREBALL INSIDE A WOODEN AIRSHIP.**  Some readers keep trying to make this more nuanced than it was. Waluigi sees this in retrospective commentary all the time.  - “Tension was already high.” - “The tactical environment was unstable.” - “Archie had seconds to decide.”  Wonderful. Lovely. All true.  And the decision was still *“fireball in a wood box in the sky.”*  Disaster Inc.’s reputation calcified in that moment. They became the group who could end a smuggling network in an afternoon and set half the deck’s expectations of physical law on fire in the process.  Waluigi’s enduring theory is that this was the first moment the universe decided not to stop them because it had become too curious to see what would happen next.  Green T, the Syndicate, and the First Redemption Arc  The Tea Leaf Syndicate’s collapse is usually told as Archie’s story.  This is wrong.  It is Green T’s story.  Archie destroyed the structure.  Green T survived the destruction.  That’s the more impressive act.  Three days after the fireball, the Syndicate made its last stand, and Green T revealed his giant form. Waluigi still thinks this reveal should be studied by anyone interested in the weaponization of underestimation. For days, Green T had been moving through rooms as an elegant criminal administrator, soft-spoken and composed, while carrying the ability to become architecturally relevant at will.  That is not merely a combat ability.  That is a philosophy.  Green T had spent his entire career letting other people misread him.  When the reveal came, it was not just strength.  It was narrative revenge.  Then Earl Grey exploded, which stole some of Green T’s thunder and part of Waluigi’s replacement hat. But Green T persisted. That is his defining trait across the whole campaign. He persists through humiliation, displacement, mirror abduction, vampire etiquette, and the loss of entire worlds of influence.  Disaster Inc. absorbed Green T not because they forgave him in some soft dramatic sense, but because he kept reappearing at the exact point where brutal competence was required.  That is how this group recruits.  Not through vows.  Through demonstrated usefulness during surreal emergencies.  The Shape of Their Morality  People keep asking if Disaster Inc. are heroes.  Waluigi hates this question because it assumes morality is a costume category.  They are not heroes the way Mario is a hero in children’s stories. They do not represent virtue, order, or aspirational plumbing.  They lie. They steal. They trespass. They improvise ethically in ways that would make legal scholars burst into tears.  But there are patterns.  They consistently move toward the trapped, the trafficked, the threatened, the eaten, the voted-upon, the left-behind.  They do not do this cleanly. They do it late. They do it while also stealing cutlery or insulting royalty or setting drapery on fire.  But they do it.  That matters.  Waluigi has been around enough “legitimate” institutions to know that a clean process can still produce evil if the people inside it are dead at the center. Disaster Inc. is the reverse. Dirty methods. Compromised people. Repeatedly correct instinct at the point where suffering becomes undeniable.  Waluigi calls this **reflexive morality**.  They do not build moral systems. They flinch toward the right thing when it becomes impossible not to see.  This is not ideal.  It is, however, often more real than the alternative.  Raventree Manor and the Transition from Adventure to Catastrophe  Before Raventree, Disaster Inc. was dangerous in the ordinary way. Smuggling crackdowns, gang violence, dragons, factional betrayals. The scale was severe but still worldly.  Raventree changed the scale.  The manor revealed a different category of threat: not a monster *in* a house, but a house that was itself participating in the violence. This distinction matters because traditional adventuring logic breaks down when your map is an enemy.  The first night there established several principles Waluigi wishes everyone had taken more seriously.  The ghost in the parlor was polite. This should have alarmed everyone more than it did. Hostile ghosts are obvious. Polite ghosts are institutional.  The toad servant who appeared with tea and a promise of clothes should also have alarmed everyone. People keep acting like service in haunted locations is comforting. It is not. Service implies routine. Routine implies a functioning social order. A functioning social order in a dead manor means something has had time to normalize the horror.  Then Markop was locked in a closet and assaulted by his own clothing.  People laugh when they summarize this. Waluigi does not. Animated garments are not random comedy. They are targeted humiliation. Raventree attacks through identity. Mirrors, doubles, wrong reflections, clothes turning on their wearer—these are not disconnected effects. The manor wants to destabilize your sense of self before it kills you.  Waluigi noticed.  Nobody listened.  Then came the Siege of Raventree, and the manor confirmed the theory by attacking everybody equally.  This is why Waluigi insists Raventree Manor is not just a location.  It is a participant.  A location with preferences. A structure with appetite.  And still the party stayed.  Because of course they did.  The Spider Grove and the Last “Normal” Nightmare  The Spider Grove was a nightmare, but it was a comprehensible nightmare. A giant matriarch. A nest. A rescue. This is the sort of thing stories understand.  What the battle reveals about Disaster Inc. is more important than the spider itself.  When the enemy is concrete, they become better. They stop acting like a sack of unrelated bad habits and start acting like a machine.  Markop becomes central pressure and control. Remi holds the line. Waluigi shapes the terrain with ice and arcane precision. The Oracle contributes impossible support in just enough quantities to remain suspicious. Mossy bites on command. Eager, absurdly, uses pepper spray on spiders and it works.  This is the party at its most functional: not sane, not disciplined, but synchronized.  Waluigi’s role in that battle matters and should be recorded correctly because people keep flattening it into *“support fire.”*  No.  Waluigi was not ornamental artillery.  Waluigi was **terrain control.**  Waluigi made movement possible through a space designed to immobilize. Frozen corridors through webs. Joint-targeting arcane rays to destabilize a giant predator under titan-scale pressure. Waluigi created options for other people’s heroics to happen.  That is not a minor contribution.  That is battle architecture.  If anyone disputes this, Waluigi invites them to fight a building-sized spider without corridor access and see how quickly they change their tone.  The Iron Legion, the Vigilance, and the Proof That Disaster Inc. Needed Enemies  Some groups are defined by ideals.  Disaster Inc. is also defined by opposition.  The Iron Legion sharpened them.  When the Legion seized the Vigilance, they did more than steal a ship. They took the shared space in which all the party’s adjacent loyalties could overlap. The Liberated Toads lost home. Bones went deep under. Ryan jumped rather than be captured.  The loss of the Vigilance turned Disaster Inc. from a mobile collective into a dispersed survival network.  Then Aegis Command and Order 120 happened, and after that the entire moral weather of the campaign changed.  Waluigi will not repeat the full horror here. Other pages have the details. The point, for Disaster Inc., is that after Order 120 there were fewer illusions left. Fewer narratives where the enemy could still be reasoned with. Fewer futures in which everybody sat down afterward and worked out terms.  The Legion made the stakes administrative and total.  That does something to a group already operating on reflexive morality. It hardens them. It makes compromise feel obscene.  Waluigi watched this happen from the edges of multiple theaters, and it is one of the reasons Disaster Inc. stopped feeling like an adventuring party and started feeling like a survival organ for everyone near them.  The Planar Fracture and the Three Separate Versions of the Group  The Oracle’s synchronization ritual was an attempt to solve the Raventree problem by aligning its fractured realities. The problem with this plan was not merely that it failed. The problem was that the plan required trust, consistency, complete participation, stable magical foundations, and someone to listen when Waluigi objected.  The ritual had none of those things.  Waluigi said so.  Waluigi got shushed.  Reality shattered.  This was the moment Disaster Inc. ceased being one party in practical terms. After the Planar Fracture, Disaster Inc. became three simultaneous field experiments in how different combinations of the same personalities function under different laws of reality.  And that, for a historian, is valuable.  For everyone living through it, it was awful.  #Disaster Inc. in the Feywild  The Feywild group forced a different arrangement of strengths.  Waluigi became less combat utility and more social hazard navigation. Toad Lee became indispensable because he could move carefully through a system where one wrong response to a flower might bind your future firstborn to a butterfly court. Hjumpik remained Hjumpik, which is to say durable, direct, and mysteriously competent in environments that should have punished his bluntness. Wario remained Wario, proving that greed is dimensionally stable.  The Feywild revealed an important internal truth: when the party enters systems built on implication, Waluigi and Toad Lee become more central than the louder personalities.  This does not mean Archie or Bowser are less valuable. It means value is environment-specific.  In the Feywild, every sentence is a tripwire. Waluigi is good with tripwires.  Waluigi has spent his whole life speaking in rooms where one wrong tone gets you laughed out of the event. Fairy courts are not actually that different from upper-class sporting ceremonies. The costumes are worse, but the danger of saying too much is familiar.  Waluigi suspects nobody else sees this parallel.  Waluigi sees it.  Waluigi sees everything.  #Disaster Inc. in the Shadowfell  The Shadowfell group became a unit of brutal directness under conditions of magical deprivation and aristocratic threat.  Archie, stripped of fire, was forced into improvisation and disguise. This is dangerous because when Archie is forced away from his core method, he gets creative, and Archie’s creativity is a public safety issue.  Bowser became the physically stabilizing force—doors, impact, confidence, refusal to be impressed by vampires. Green T became the precision instrument, which culminated in the silver-bullet shot and the destruction of the Shadow Anchor.  Then Vivian escalated.  Vivian’s revelation as both Vivesna and vivian_corvinarus changes how Waluigi interprets the entire Shadowfell arc. People think the danger *“arrived.”* It did not. It infiltrated, observed, learned, and then took off the servant mask when the conditions were right.  This means the Shadowfell team was being studied from inside the house by a future claimant with superior local knowledge and nonstandard magic.  That is not bad luck.  That is strategic asymmetry.  It also makes the ordinary details more sinister. The maintenance corridors. The normal vegetables. The library routines. The infirmary. The Archivist’s deal with Toadburt. This is not just a haunted vampire palace. It is an operating institution in the middle of a succession war.  Institutions are always worse than monsters because monsters are honest about what they want.  #Disaster Inc. in the Deep Mirror  The Deep Mirror group demonstrates the most frightening version of Disaster Inc.: the version where there is no external structure at all and they still somehow continue.  Markop and Remi, with the Oracle as their guide or manipulator or both, entered a dimension where even basic assumptions like down and later stopped being reliable.  And still they kept moving.  This is where Waluigi’s respect for Markop and concern for Remi deepened most sharply. Markop’s ability to function under collapsing spatial logic confirms something Waluigi already believed: if there is a person in the party most likely to remain tactically coherent after reality itself stops cooperating, it is Markop.  Remi’s survival there confirms something uglier: she keeps paying from herself to remain useful.  Disaster Inc. depends on this kind of survival.  Waluigi hates that it does.  The Material World Consequences  While Disaster Inc. was scattered across planes, the Material world did not pause politely.  It got worse.  #Iron Sky Breach  The Iron Legion boarded and took the Vigilance with mechanical precision. Ryan jumped. Bones went undercover.  The capture of the Vigilance matters to Disaster Inc. because it removed the one stable hub that kept the party’s extended network connected.  Without the Vigilance, Disaster Inc. became truly scattered, not just across dimensions but across logistics.  No shared storage. No shared safe space. No shared meeting point.  This is when Waluigi’s documentation became critical. When infrastructure collapses, history collapses next.  The Legion didn’t just take a ship.  They took the story-control platform.  Waluigi hated that.  #Massacre at Aegis (Order 120)  Order 120 killed prisoners as an administrative response to embarrassment.  Waluigi does not make jokes about this. Waluigi has plenty of jokes. He does not use them here.  But in terms of Disaster Inc. dynamics, Order 120 created something that later affected everything: it hardened the Liberated Toads, radicalized Speaker L, and made the overall crisis less negotiable.  When an enemy is willing to execute prisoners as paperwork, you stop believing in compromise.  And when compromise dies, everything becomes war.  #The Vigilance Crisis  Dan’s breakdown and the staff catastrophe is technically a Liberated Toads event, but it matters to Disaster Inc. because Green T’s actions and Toad Lee’s leadership become part of the group’s extended survival web.  Green T’s redemption is not emotional. It is operational. He proved he would bleed for others.  Toad Lee’s staff seizure proves he can make hard decisions under pressure.  These are traits Disaster Inc. needs around them, because Disaster Inc. is constantly in situations where hesitation kills.  Member Roles During the Fracture  This is where Disaster Inc. stops being *“a party”* and becomes *“a distributed organism.”*  Each member’s role shifted based on environment.  #Waluigi Navigator, social defense, pattern-reader in the Feywild.  #Toad Lee Stabilizer, obligation-filter, quiet survival strategist.  #Hjumpik Brute survival engine, work ethic, Orange Alignment participant.  #Wario Loot, explosives, logistics, greed made useful.  #Archie Infiltrator by necessity because his fire was suppressed and therefore he had to use his brain, which is always dangerous because Archie’s brain thinks fire is a persuasive argument.  #Bowser Frontline siege weapon and bodyguard.  #Green T Assassin and tactical operator.  #Markop Anchor in environments that tried to dissolve anchors.  #Remi The human cost ledger—surviving, adapting, and trading pieces of herself for continued motion.  The Current Internal Hierarchy (The One Nobody Admits Exists)  Disaster Inc. insists it has no leader.  This is technically true.  It is also incomplete.  The group has what Waluigi would call a **context hierarchy.**  When violence becomes immediate and tactical, **Markop rises.**  When emotional collapse threatens group cohesion, **Toad Lee rises.**  When physical force is the only language left, **Bowser rises.**  When infiltration, deception, or hidden violence becomes necessary, **Green T rises.**  When logistics must be conjured from greed and wreckage, **Wario rises.**  When magical terrain needs shaping or patterns need noticing, **Waluigi rises.**  When catastrophe needs a face, **Archie rises**, usually unintentionally.  The group functions because these shifts happen fast. Nobody calls a vote. Nobody states, *“Markop has command now.”* The room simply turns.  That is more sophisticated than the party admits.  Waluigi suspects the refusal to formalize this is partly superstition. Name the structure and something will try to kill it.  Given the campaign so far, this is not irrational.  Secondary Orbit: The People Around Disaster Inc.  A party this unstable develops gravitational zones.  The Liberated Toads are not part of Disaster Inc., but they are tied to it through repeated crisis overlap, mutual aid, and the original sin of the barrel discovery. Toad Lee becomes the bridge. Green T’s redemption arc intersects with them hard during the Vigilance Crisis. Dan’s collapse, the vow, Speaker L’s demands—these all become Disaster Inc.-adjacent because the party keeps stepping into the center of systems in distress.  Eager exists in the orbit as a chaos attractor. Waluigi says this with reluctant affection. Eager has a supernatural ability to be where the plot is thickest and the floor is least trustworthy. He is not the group’s strategist. He is the group’s accidental tripwire. Valuable in his own way. Exhausting in everyone else’s.  Bones exists as proof that sometimes competence wears a quiet face. Ryan exists as proof that bravery and desperation often look identical from a distance. Roger exists as proof that poison can solve problems and create trauma simultaneously. Creek exists as proof that there are always medics somewhere in the rubble if you are lucky enough to ask loudly.  The Oracle exists in all of this like a hand in dirty water: visible only by the things it disturbs.  Waluigi does not trust the Oracle.  Waluigi has not trusted the Oracle from the beginning.  The Oracle keeps being useful.  This does not improve trust.  Theories Waluigi Has Seen Evidence For  Waluigi is including this section because if he dies, people will call these ideas delusions, and then twenty sessions later someone will find Waluigi was right and act surprised.  Waluigi hates this cycle.  #Theory One: Disaster Inc. Is Itself a Balancing Structure  Not metaphorically.  Metaphysically.  The group’s composition is too strange. Fire and ice. Greed and restraint. Brute force and precision. Opportunist and conscience. Titan and infiltrator. They repeatedly end up in exactly the places where some equilibrium needs to be restored, broken, exposed, or forced into motion.  People say this is because they are protagonists.  Waluigi rejects this explanation because it is lazy.  Waluigi suspects the repeated coalescence of these specific personalities around planar stress points means the group itself has become a balancing pattern. A living, accidental sigil. Not chosen, not ordained, but repeatedly arranged by the same larger structures because the universe has decided this ugly configuration produces movement.  Nobody believes this because it sounds mystical.  But the alternative is coincidence, and coincidence has been overworked.  #Theory Two: Archie Is More Than Unstable — He Is Resonant  People treat Archie’s magic as chaotic.  Waluigi thinks this is incomplete.  Archie’s magic doesn’t just misfire. It **catches.** It hooks into unstable environments and amplifies whatever fault lines are already there.  - The Tea Party Incident - The ritual fracture - The manor escalation  Archie’s fire behaves like a tuning fork for structural weakness.  This means Archie is not simply a hazard.  He is a detector.  A horribly destructive detector.  No one likes this theory because it implies Archie is indispensable in a way that justifies Archie, and nobody wants to justify Archie.  Waluigi is not justifying him.  Waluigi is describing him.  #Theory Three: Green T Has Been Underestimated So Consistently That Reality Now Cooperates With the Bit  Waluigi is only half joking here.  Green T’s arc has passed beyond normal probability. Too many humiliations converted too efficiently into tactical advantage. Too many losses turned into cleaner, deadlier forms of presence.  The children’s table becoming a sniper nest is the perfect expression of this.  Waluigi thinks Green T has become the patron saint of being dismissed at exactly the wrong moment.  This is not a recognized metaphysical office.  It should be.  #Theory Four: There Is Still One Layer of Raventree Nobody Has Mapped  Waluigi already wrote about the possibility of a fourth reflection, but he will say it again because it matters.  The structure of the manor does not resolve cleanly into Material, Fey, Shadow, and Deep Mirror.  The Deep Mirror feels like runoff. Like a pressure basin. Like overflow.  There is another layer. A hidden one, or a sealed one, or a reflection that only appears under conditions not yet met.  Waluigi has seen brief geometry in mirrors that matched none of the known states.  Nobody believes him.  Good.  That means fewer fools will go looking before there’s a plan.  #Theory Five: The Party Survives Partly Because Everyone Underestimates How Much Waluigi Is Doing  This is less a theory and more a recurring observable pattern.  Waluigi notices the corridor before it closes. Waluigi reads the room before the fight starts. Waluigi controls the battlefield so the heroes can be heroes in a shape the bards understand.  History likes central figures.  Reality likes utility.  Waluigi is utility wrapped in beauty.  History will catch up eventually.  Present State: Fragmented, Functioning, Furious  Disaster Inc. at present is not one body.  It is one will in multiple pieces.  The Shadowfell branch is under immediate pressure from Vivian, institutional entanglements, entropy-ring threats, and the unstable internal politics of the Onyx Hand.  The Feywild branch remains trapped in a system where every bargain accumulates debt and every debt has flowers on it.  The Deep Mirror branch exists in relation to the Sanctum and whatever the Oracle is trying to make of collapsed timelines.  The Material world continues to spin beneath all this, with the Iron Legion occupying key infrastructure, the Regency trying to govern through consensus while the world burns faster than committees can schedule meetings, the Peach Loyalists becoming more effective and more frightening, and the Liberated Toads trying to build community from repeated devastation.  And through all of this, Disaster Inc. remains what it has always been:  - Not orderly - Not clean - Not sane  But **present.**  That matters more than most political analysts understand. Presence is power. Showing up in the impossible place and refusing to leave is a kind of strategy all its own.  Disaster Inc. keeps doing it.  They keep being where the fracture is widest, where the horror is thickest, where the institution has failed, where the monster is largest, where the dinner invitation should clearly have been declined.  They keep going.  Waluigi does not know whether this is courage, stupidity, mutual dependence, or the simple inability to imagine stopping.  It may be all four.  Waluigi respects it anyway.  And now Waluigi is going to state the part nobody else will write because they are too sentimental or too embarrassed:  **Disaster Inc. is not lovable.**  Disaster Inc. is not admirable in the clean sense.  Disaster Inc. is dangerous to know, expensive to help, socially disastrous, morally inconsistent, physically destructive, and a catastrophic influence on furniture.  But if the world survives the present crisis, a significant percentage of that survival will trace back to moments where Disaster Inc. walked into a place they should never have entered and refused to let the worst thing in the room remain unchallenged.  This is not the same as innocence.  It may, however, be enough.  Waluigi has spent his whole life being the one people notice too late. Too tall, too strange, too sharp-edged for the happy narratives, too useful to dismiss once the floor starts collapsing.  That is why Waluigi understands Disaster Inc. better than anyone else does.  The world likes easy categories.  - Heroes - Villains - Criminals - Victims - Kings - Toads - Monsters  Disaster Inc. ruins categories.  That is why history will struggle to tell their story.  That is also why Waluigi had to write it.  Because if you leave the story to cleaner hands, they will wash out the truth.  The truth is ugly. The truth is loud. The truth smells faintly of smoke, spider ichor, vampire candle wax, sewer lava, old tea, bad decisions, and one very expensive hat that never deserved what happened to it.  The truth is that Disaster Inc. should have died several times already and did not.  Waluigi has stopped calling that luck.  Waluigi now calls it **trajectory.**  And the trajectory is still moving.  **WAH.**

name: The DK Crew
title: Kongo Bongo's Finest (And Lankiest)
region: Kongo Bongo Island and surrounding territories
status: Active — diplomatically bruised after Second Summit, but intact
leader: Donkey Kong (nominal), Cranky Kong (actual authority on everything)
motto: Waluigi doesn't think they have a formal motto, but it probably involves bananas
summary: The DK Crew is the extended Kong family and their allies—a loose coalition of primates who defend Kongo Bongo Island from Kremling incursions and occasionally participate in regional diplomacy with mixed results. At the Second Summit, DK walked out after Dedede's ego explosion, which was the RIGHT call but created cascade effects that damaged the whole event. Waluigi respects DK's principles. Waluigi wishes those principles had better TIMING.
description:
Waluigi needs to explain the DK Crew because they're important regional players who get dismissed as 'just the banana people' by factions that should know better.

Structure (Such As It Is)

The DK Crew is less a formal organization and more an extended family that fights together. Donkey Kong is the strongest and most recognizable, so people assume he's the leader. Cranky Kong is the oldest and most cantankerous, so he ACTS like the leader regardless of what anyone else thinks. Diddy Kong is DK's most reliable partner. Dixie Kong brings tactical flexibility and hair-based combat capabilities. Funky Kong handles logistics and apparently SECRET FOOTAGE of Kremling operations.

Then there's Lanky Kong. Waluigi has FEELINGS about Lanky.

Lanky is not incompetent. Lanky is AWKWARD in ways that enemies can exploit. At the Second Summit, the Kremlings identified Lanky as a chaos vector and systematically provoked him until he slapped someone on camera, giving them exactly the propaganda footage they wanted. Lanky got PLAYED, and the whole crew's reputation suffered for it.

Waluigi has BEEN the person who gets played. Waluigi has been the awkward one whose mistakes get magnified while everyone else's get ignored. Waluigi SYMPATHIZES with Lanky even while recognizing that Lanky's actions created real problems.

The Summit Walkout

DK's walkout from the Second Summit was structurally inevitable once Dedede crossed certain lines. You can't sit through a speech that personally humiliates you and your delegation and then pretend everything's fine. Walking out was the dignified response.

The PROBLEM was that DK's walkout triggered a cascade. Once one major delegation left, others followed—not because they all agreed with DK, but because the NORMS had collapsed. Staying started to look like endorsement of whatever was happening. Leaving started to look reasonable.

DK didn't intend to crash the summit. But actions have consequences beyond intent, and DK's principled stand contributed to a diplomatic mess that hurt everyone involved.

Waluigi respects the principle. Waluigi wishes the timing had been different. But Waluigi also knows you can't always control timing—sometimes you have to act when the moment demands, consequences be damned.

The Funky Footage

Funky Kong has footage that apparently shows the Kremling operation at the summit—the deliberate provocations, the setup, the calculated baiting of Lanky. This footage could reframe the entire narrative around the summit incident, shifting blame from Lanky to the Kremlings who manufactured the crisis.

The footage hasn't been released yet. It's a weapon that only works once—release it too early and people dismiss it as damage control, release it too late and nobody cares anymore. The Kongs are presumably deciding on optimal timing.

Waluigi hopes they use it well. The Kremlings deserve to have their operation exposed. But Waluigi also knows that counter-narratives are harder to spread than original narratives. The Kremlings got their story out first.

Assessment

The DK Crew is more capable than regional politics gives them credit for. They've defended Kongo Bongo against Kremling incursions for YEARS. They maintain functional governance and social structures. They participate in international events even when those events go badly.

Their weakness is sophistication—not in the condescending sense, but in the literal sense that they're not optimized for the kind of information warfare and diplomatic maneuvering that other factions engage in. They're DIRECT. They punch problems. This works great against Kremlings; it works less great against Kremling PROPAGANDA.

Waluigi recommends the DK Crew hire a communications specialist. Someone who can help them navigate media environments the way DK navigates jungle environments. They need someone who understands that in modern conflicts, punching the enemy is only half the battle—you also have to win the narrative about the punching.

Waluigi would volunteer, but Waluigi is busy. Also, Waluigi's communication style might not be what they're looking for. Waluigi is DISTINCTIVE.

WAH.

name: The Koopa Troop
title: Bowser's Army (When He Remembers He Has One)
region: Koopa Kingdom, with operations across Mushroom Kingdom territories
status: Active but fragmented — Bowser's dimensional displacement has complicated command structure
headquarters: Bowser's Castle (primary), various fortresses throughout the region
motto: Waluigi has heard several versions, none of them inspiring confidence
summary: The Koopa Troop is Bowser's military force—an army of Goombas, Koopas, Hammer Bros, and various other species united primarily by loyalty to their king. In peacetime, they're the Mushroom Kingdom's most reliable antagonist. In the current crisis, they're a wild card—Bowser's dimensional displacement in the Shadowfell has left the Troop operating without clear direction, some units allying with Disaster Inc., others pursuing independent agendas. Waluigi has complicated feelings about the Troop because Waluigi has PLAYED SPORTS with these people.
description:
Waluigi needs to address the Koopa Troop because they're both more and less important than people assume.

Organizational Reality

The Koopa Troop is theoretically a professional military force with clear hierarchy, strategic objectives, and coordinated operations. In REALITY, the Troop is a collection of semi-independent units held together primarily by Bowser's personality and the fact that nobody wants to be the one who has to tell Bowser his army fell apart.

Bowser commands through force of presence. When Bowser is THERE—loud, huge, breathing fire—nobody questions orders. Units coordinate. Objectives get pursued. The machinery functions.

When Bowser is NOT there—as in his current Shadowfell displacement—the machinery starts grinding. Kamek tries to hold things together, but Kamek is an advisor, not a king. The Koopalings have their own agendas. Regional commanders start making independent decisions. What was an army becomes a collection of armies that happen to share uniforms.

Current Status

Bowser's involvement with Disaster Inc. has further complicated Troop operations. Bowser personally ally-ing with the party that SHATTERED REALITY creates awkward questions for Troop commanders who aren't sure if their king has lost his mind or discovered new strategic opportunities.

Some units have followed Bowser's apparent lead and cooperated with Disaster Inc. operations. Others have continued pursuing traditional Koopa Troop objectives—territory, resources, opposition to Mushroom Kingdom governance. Still others have gone essentially independent, pursuing local goals without reference to kingdom-level strategy.

The Iron Legion has exploited this fragmentation, picking off isolated Koopa Troop positions while the overall force lacks coordination to respond. The Legion is systematic; the Troop is chaotic. Systematic beats chaotic in grinding territorial conflict.

Waluigi's History

Waluigi has played sports with Koopa Troop members. Tennis. Go-karts. Party games of various descriptions. On the field, they're COMPETITORS—aggressive, determined, occasionally dirty in ways Waluigi recognizes and respects.

Off the field, they're just PEOPLE. Goombas with families. Koopas with hobbies. Hammer Bros who argue about football and complain about their commanding officers. Waluigi has had conversations with Troop members that had nothing to do with conquest or conflict—just normal people talking about normal things.

This makes the current situation complicated. These are people Waluigi knows. People Waluigi has competed against. People who probably don't want war any more than anyone else but are caught up in systems bigger than their individual choices.

Waluigi doesn't hate the Koopa Troop. Waluigi hates WAR, and the Koopa Troop happens to be part of several wars. But the individual soldiers are just soldiers. They follow orders because that's what soldiers do. Judging them for that seems unfair when the alternative is judging the entire concept of military service.

Assessment

The Koopa Troop will remain a significant force regardless of the current crisis's outcome. They have infrastructure, population, institutional knowledge, and a king who WILL return from the Shadowfell eventually (Bowser always comes back).

The question is what kind of force they'll be when things stabilize. Will Bowser's experience with Disaster Inc. change his strategic thinking? Will the fragmentation during his absence create lasting fractures? Will the Troop emerge stronger for having survived leadership disruption, or weaker for having experienced it?

Waluigi doesn't know. Waluigi does know that whatever happens, he'll probably end up playing tennis against them again eventually. Waluigi hopes the courts survive that long.

WAH.

name: Liberated Toads
title: Survivors of the Vigilance
leader: Toad Lee and Rodger (co-leaders), Speaker L (150 freed toads)
summary: The Liberated Toads are what happens when ordinary people get caught between empires and survive anyway. Over 150 trafficked toads were found hidden in barrels across the Vigilance—BARRELS, like cargo, like OBJECTS—and the community that formed from those survivors became one of the most important factions in the entire crisis. Recent events aboard the Vigilance pushed the faction to the breaking point: Dan's mental breakdown, a fireball that killed thirteen toads, a staff that nearly consumed souls, and a political crisis that required binding oaths to resolve. Waluigi has complicated feelings about the Liberated Toads because watching good people suffer while powerful people play political games makes Waluigi ANGRY in a way that goes deeper than his usual anger.
description:
The discovery of the barrel toads was one of the moments that changed everything aboard the Vigilance. Over 150 toads, individually packed into barrels, hidden throughout the ship as part of a trafficking operation so methodical and so dehumanizing that even WARIO was disturbed, and Wario's moral compass points toward whatever direction has the most coins.

Waluigi was there when the first barrels were opened. He saw the condition those toads were in. He doesn't talk about it much because some things don't get better by talking about them. What he WILL say is that anyone who traffics people in barrels deserves whatever comes to them, and Waluigi's definition of 'whatever' is more creative than most people's.

Formation and Early Days

The Liberated Toads formed organically—not as a political movement or a military force, but as a community of survivors trying to figure out what happens NEXT when 'next' isn't something anyone planned for. They had been cargo. Now they were people again. The transition was not smooth.

Leadership coalesced around two poles: Speaker L, who pushed for organization, accountability, and structured response to threats; and Dan, who advocated for collective survival strategies, caution, and not rushing into fights that the faction couldn't win.

The Vigilance Crisis

Recent events aboard the Vigilance nearly tore the faction apart.

It began with chaos. Green T warned of a fungal infestation. Toad Lee and Rodger asserted themselves as co-leaders, but Green T attempted to seize control, offering himself as interim leader with Purple T as co-leader. Toad Lee countered by rallying toads around Rodger. The 'Class of T'—Teacher T, Bully T, Nerd T, and Geek T—all pledged their support, strengthening Rodger's position.

Trust remained fragile. Toad Lee openly told Green T he didn't trust him but agreed to test his loyalty by ordering him to disarm a Crown Intelligence agent aboard. 'I trust you... a little,' Toad Lee admitted.

When Rodger and Ryan distributed their meager weapon stockpile—two short swords, a longsword, and a club—to 150 desperate toads, chaos erupted. Fights broke out over who would be armed. A toad was knocked unconscious. Bones had to shout to restore order. The ship nearly devolved into civil war over four weapons.

After five minutes of arguing, the toads elected a representative who delivered a speech that Waluigi found surprisingly moving: 'It's about time we take a stand! It stinks to live in a world where toads finish last. No more being pushed around—not even by other toads!'

Dan's Breakdown and the Staff Crisis

Then Dan arrived.

Dan had snuck away to the Vigilance separately, driven by something he wouldn't explain. When he appeared in the engine room, he was broken—clutching his mage staff, apologizing, collapsing to his knees. Green T struck him while he was down. Dan defended with the staff, hurling Green T into the crowd. The mob turned on Green T, clawing at him.

In desperation, Dan unleashed a forcefield, blasting toads aside. Then came the fireball.

**Thirteen toads died in flames.**

The staff's corruption bled into Dan. He almost devoured the souls of the fallen, absorbing one soul of compassion into the staff before negotiations could halt him. Dan was going mad, and the Liberated Toads were caught between his power and their own survival.

Green T, damaged but determined, crawled to Toad Lee and bargained. Against all odds, he wrested the staff from Dan—even chopping off Dan's arm to do so. When Green T tried to claim the staff for himself, Toad Lee struck him down and seized it.

To everyone's shock, Toad Lee acknowledged Green T's sacrifice: 'You proved yourself trustworthy.'

Dan lay bleeding, armless. Creek, a toad who had worked as a medic at a hospital, stepped forward to stabilize him. Purple T, bruised but alive, rejoined the group. Green T was taken to receive treatment alongside Dan.

The Thirteen Demands

With the immediate crisis resolved, a new one emerged. Speaker L—the vengeful toad who had beaten down all rivals to lead the 150 freed captives—declared that his people would not simply join the Liberated Toads. They presented thirteen non-negotiable demands:

1. Full and equal voting rights within the council
2. Guaranteed housing and rations equal to or greater than original members
3. A 'Trauma and Reparations Fund' from the party's treasury
4. A formal public apology from Lario, with 30% of his workshop's future profits garnished for the fund
5. A formal public apology from Archie for reckless behavior; barred from unsupervised engine room access
6. Immediate destruction of the Iron Binding seal on X.O.'s staff
7. Guaranteed representation in all diplomatic negotiations
8. Creation of a 'Toad's Landing Security Force' staffed exclusively by their members
9. Priority access to all medical supplies
10. The right to refuse high-risk missions without penalty
11. Formal recognition as the 'Second Founding' with co-equal leadership status
12. Immediate pursuit and prosecution of the Freelancers responsible for their capture—no deals, no ransoms
13. A really, really nice hat with a feather for Speaker L (non-negotiable)

The existing leadership could not accept all demands. Counter-offers were made:

- **Voting:** Observer status with 2 advisory votes for 6 months, reviewable for elevation
- **Housing:** Shared quarters and standard rations equal to other recruits
- **Reparations:** A community rebuilding program with work-based contributions instead of draining the treasury
- **Iron Binding:** A joint oversight committee with freed toad representation, not immediate destruction
- **Recognition:** 'First Cohort of Renewal' with ceremonial honors, leadership parity deferred until trust is earned

The Vote

The 137 voting toads split:

**YES (78 votes):** Most younger toads, the 'Class of T' group, and those yearning for unity. Teacher T demanded the vow be magically bound. Bully T promised 'first swing' against any oathbreaker. Nerd T wanted every decision recorded. Geek T worried the vow might corrupt them. Purple T voted yes but grumbled about nearly being killed by trusting Green T.

**NO (59 votes):** Hardened fighters, especially those angry about Dan's fireball killing thirteen toads. Survivors shouted 'Vows won't fix broken bones!' A group led by a scarred toad argued the staff itself was cursed. One toad demanded 'Who watches the watchers?'

The Vow Ceremony

Speaker L raised his feathered hat high and declared:

*'This vow binds us, but remember—I lead because I won that right. If anyone dares betray it, you betray me. And I will answer betrayal with fury.'*

The crowd murmured—half in fear, half in respect.

Toad Lee held the staff aloft, trembling, as each representative placed a hand on the floor. L intoned:

*'We swear: to guard the staff, never to abuse it, never to let it fall into enemy hands. We swear not to betray one another, lest the Liberated Toads fall to ruin.'*

A faint shimmer ran along the staff as if the vow itself was acknowledged.

Rodger delivered the final response:

*'We accept the vow. We'll guard the staff with competence, with caution, and with loyalty to the Liberated Toads. But know this—if any hand falters, if any word twists the vow, we will tear that traitor down ourselves.'*

The hall erupted in croaks of applause.

Current Status

The Liberated Toads are reorganized but scarred. Dan is incapacitated—shrunk, armless, and recovering under the archmage's care. Green T has proven himself trustworthy and now operates as an ally. The 150 freed toads have integrated under the terms of the vow, with Speaker L commanding their loyalty. The staff remains a dangerous asset, bound by oath but still corrupted.

Waluigi watches the Liberated Toads and sees a faction that has been through more than any group should endure. Trafficked. Freed. Organized. Nearly destroyed from within by madness and fire. Still standing. Still bound by oath. Whether that oath holds under pressure remains to be seen. WAH.

name: Iron Legion
title: The Midlands War Machine
region: The Midlands, expanding into Mushroom Kingdom territories
summary: The Iron Legion is the faction Waluigi hates most, and Waluigi has a COMPREHENSIVE hate list organized by category, severity, and whether the target has ever personally insulted his hat. The Legion is a former mercenary company that evolved into a military superpower with the moral compass of a filing cabinet. They are ruthless, efficient, bureaucratic, and treat human beings as logistical variables. They stole the Vigilance, murdered prisoners under Order 120, and broadcast propaganda at Waluigi during a GIANT SPIDER FIGHT. Waluigi will never forgive them for any of it.
description:
The Iron Legion started as a mercenary company in the Midlands, which tells Waluigi everything he needs to know about the Midlands' taste in organizations. They were hired muscle who decided they'd rather BE the client than serve one, and through a combination of military competence, political maneuvering, and a total absence of ethical hesitation, they transformed into a state-level power.

Waluigi has a grudging respect for competence. He does NOT have respect for what the Iron Legion does with that competence. They use spies, boarding actions, false flag operations, interrogation, emergency legislation, and administrative murder with equal facility. They are the kind of organization that will infiltrate your group, steal your ship, kill your prisoners, and FILE PAPERWORK about all of it. Waluigi has met villains who at least have the decency to be DRAMATIC about their villainy. The Iron Legion commits atrocities and then updates a spreadsheet.

Structure and Methods

The Legion operates on rigid hierarchy, protocol-driven decision-making, and institutional discipline that borders on the mechanical. Every soldier knows their place. Every operation follows procedure. Every prisoner gets a case number. The system's strength is its reliability—it does not depend on individual brilliance, charisma, or morale. It depends on everyone following orders, and the Legion's training ensures that orders are followed.

This is also its weakness, as Bones demonstrated during his infiltration of Aegis Command. The system assumes that anyone in the right uniform following the right protocols belongs. It doesn't account for individuals who can fake the uniform and the protocols because the system was designed by people who cannot imagine someone WANTING to be anything other than a compliant Legionnaire.

Waluigi finds the Iron Legion's institutional personality deeply disturbing. They don't hate their enemies. Hatred would require emotional investment. They PROCESS their enemies. They categorize threats, allocate resources, execute solutions, and move to the next item on the agenda. When General Ironhand signed Order 120—the execution of all Toad prisoners—he wasn't acting out of rage or vengeance. He was managing a security breach. The prisoners were a variable that needed to be eliminated from the equation. The fact that the variables were PEOPLE was, to the Legion's institutional logic, irrelevant.

That's what makes them terrifying. Not cruelty—INDIFFERENCE. They will kill you and be bored by it.

Key Operations

The Legion's operations during the 1040 BF crisis demonstrate their methodology:

- **The Iron Sky Breach:** A coordinated boarding action that captured the Vigilance—the Liberated Toads' headquarters—in a single afternoon. The operation was planned for days, timed to a shift change, and executed with mechanical precision. They renamed the ship 'Legionlance,' which Waluigi maintains is the worst name for an airship in recorded history. It sounds like a MEDICAL PROCEDURE.

- **The Iron Mandate:** Emergency legislation granting the Legion sweeping authority to purge supernatural threats. This legal framework gave their military operations a veneer of legitimacy, transforming acts of conquest into acts of 'compliance enforcement.' Waluigi has seen a lot of creative excuses for bad behavior—he once watched Wario claim tax fraud was 'aggressive financial innovation'—but the Iron Mandate is the most sophisticated he's encountered.

- **The Massacre at Aegis Command:** The event that defined the Legion's legacy. Bones infiltrated the fortress, was caught, and General Ironhand responded by ordering the execution of all Toad prisoners. Every single one. Not because they were threats. Not because they were combatants. Because Ironhand's security had been embarrassed and prisoners were a convenient target for administrative retaliation.

- **Seizure of the Ritual Room:** After the Planar Fracture shattered reality around Raventree Manor, the Legion immediately seized the physical anchor point—the only stable connection between the three planar fragments. They then deployed Toadburt into the Feywild as a coerced agent fitted with an Entropy Ring. Sending someone into an alien dimension with an obedience collar because the opportunity presented itself is PEAK Iron Legion behavior.

General Ironhand

Waluigi has a personal section about General Ironhand because Waluigi believes the world needs to understand what kind of person leads the Iron Legion.

Ironhand is not a ranting warlord. He's not a cackling villain. He doesn't make speeches about conquest or destiny or the superiority of his cause. He's a military administrator who happens to have the authority to order massacres. He stabbed Bones during interrogation with the precision of someone making a professional point. He signed Order 120 with the same pen he probably used to approve equipment requisitions that morning.

Waluigi has called many people villains in this encyclopedia. Ironhand isn't a villain. Villains have PERSONALITY. Ironhand is a SYSTEM wearing a general's uniform. He is the Iron Legion's institutional indifference given a rank and a desk, and that makes him more dangerous than any dragon or vampire lord Waluigi has ever faced.

Waluigi would like General Ironhand to go sit on a Thwomp. Waluigi would like this noted for the record. WAH.

name: Pond Patrol
title: Order, Containment, Apprehension
region: Raventree Manor vicinity and former Vigilance territories
headquarters: Mobile — field encampments around Raventree Manor
affiliation: Speaker L / Liberated Toads hardline wing
summary: The Pond Patrol is Speaker L's enforcement arm—a disciplined toad-led paramilitary force that started as a procedural investigative body and has been progressively hardened by infiltration, massacre, and the kind of betrayals that turn reasonable people into very UNREASONABLE people. Waluigi respects Speaker L. Waluigi also worries about Speaker L. Those two feelings are not contradictory.
description:
The Pond Patrol represents the organized, militant wing of the Liberated Toads' response to the world that keeps trying to kill them. Under Speaker L's leadership, the Patrol operates with a level of discipline that rivals professional military forces—structured chain of command, standard operating procedures, intelligence-gathering protocols, and accountability mechanisms that Speaker L insists upon with an intensity that borders on obsession.

Waluigi has dealt with the Pond Patrol both as an ally and as a subject of their investigations, and the experience is DIFFERENT depending on which side of their procedures you're on. When they're on your side, the Patrol is competent, reliable, and reassuringly organized. When they're investigating YOU—as they did during the Siege of Raventree when Archie was under suspicion—the Patrol is thorough, relentless, and not particularly interested in hearing your side of the story until they've finished hearing THEIR side of the story.

The Siege of Raventree

The Pond Patrol's most significant military operation was the Siege of Raventree Manor, where Speaker L surrounded the building with a containment perimeter after the failed healing attempt on Eager. The siege was competently executed—observation posts, controlled exits, clear demands delivered through amplified address. Speaker L wasn't being unreasonable. He wanted answers about what happened to Eager, he wanted Archie held accountable, and he wanted it done through structured process.

The manor, however, had its own opinions about being besieged. When Raventree Manor began spawning wraiths that attacked the Pond Patrol perimeter as aggressively as they attacked the people inside, the siege became something nobody had planned for. You can't maintain a disciplined containment operation when the building you're containing is actively trying to kill your sentries with supernatural entities.

Speaker L held his people together through the wraith attacks, which is a testament to both his leadership and the Patrol's discipline. Lesser organizations would have broken and run. The Pond Patrol held position, adjusted perimeters, and dealt with wraiths using whatever combat capabilities they had. Waluigi was impressed, and Waluigi does not impress easily because Waluigi's standards are EXTREMELY high, primarily because Waluigi himself sets those standards.

Speaker L's Transformation

The Pond Patrol's trajectory mirrors Speaker L's personal transformation. Before Order 120, the Patrol was procedural. After Order 120, it became something harder.

Speaker L was the kind of leader who believed in process. Investigate first. Gather evidence. Hold people accountable through structured proceedings. He besieged Raventree Manor not because he wanted violence but because he wanted ANSWERS, and he believed the right questions, asked through the right channels, would produce them.

Order 120 killed that belief along with every Toad prisoner in Iron Legion custody.

The Speaker L who emerged from that atrocity was grimmer, more ruthless, and no longer interested in the kinds of procedural niceties that assume the other side will reciprocate. He began chanting war anthems—not morale-boosting songs but the kind of dark, rhythmic declarations that come from someone who has decided that the world offers only two options: destroy or be destroyed.

His vow to hunt the Green Decoy—the impostor who wore his face—added a personal dimension to the Patrol's mission. The Decoy wasn't just an intelligence threat. It was someone who had used Speaker L's identity while Speaker L's people were being murdered. That kind of violation doesn't heal through process. It heals through FINDING the person responsible and making them answer for it.

Waluigi watches the Pond Patrol now and sees a faction being transformed by grief into something that might be more effective but is definitely more dangerous. They are better fighters than they were before Order 120. They are better intelligence operatives. They are harder, sharper, more willing to do difficult things. But they are also angrier, less patient, and increasingly operating under the logic that mercy is a luxury they can no longer afford.

Waluigi understands anger. Waluigi has been angry his ENTIRE LIFE. But anger without a limit becomes something else, and Waluigi hopes Speaker L finds his limit before the Pond Patrol becomes the thing it was created to oppose. WAH.

name: Mages' Guild
title: Custodians of Arcane Order (Self-Appointed)
region: Multi-regional, headquartered in the Arcane Quarter
leader: Unknown (institutional leadership, which is VERY convenient for avoiding accountability)
summary: The Mages' Guild is the kind of institution that presents itself as the responsible adult in the room while actively making the room MORE dangerous through 'research.' They study threats that their studying makes worse, they track people with magical surveillance badges, they maintain null cages for containing supernatural entities, and they have clashed repeatedly with Archie Miser, which is the ONE thing about them Waluigi finds relatable because Waluigi ALSO clashes with Archie, though Waluigi's clashes involve less bureaucracy and more shouting.
description:
Waluigi has a complicated relationship with the Mages' Guild. On one hand, they possess genuine expertise in magical theory, planar mechanics, and supernatural containment that has proven valuable during the Raventree crisis. Agent L, their primary field operative in the campaign, is competent, practical, and has on multiple occasions done genuinely heroic things. Waluigi respects Agent L as an individual.

On the other hand, the INSTITUTION is a different animal entirely. The Mages' Guild treats people the way mathematicians treat variables—as elements in an equation to be solved. They investigate phenomena with a clinical detachment that fails to account for the fact that the phenomena are happening TO PEOPLE. They study planar instability in ways that may worsen the instability. They monitor individuals with magical tracking badges without necessarily informing those individuals that they're being tracked. They maintain null cages—containment devices designed to hold supernatural entities—and seem more interested in what they can LEARN from the contained entities than in whether the containment is ethical.

Waluigi finds the Guild's moral positioning EXHAUSTING. They claim to be custodians of arcane order while conducting experiments that threaten to DISORDER everything further. They present themselves as neutral arbiters of magical law while pursuing institutional agendas that benefit the Guild's power and influence. They lecture Archie Miser about responsible magic use while their own research programs push boundaries that responsible practitioners would never approach.

Relationship with Archie Miser

The Guild and Archie have a history that predates the current crisis. Archie's magical approach—instinctive, volatile, fire-oriented, and conducted with the caution of someone who has never read a safety manual—is everything the Guild officially opposes. His confession to Guild authorities (the specifics of which Waluigi was not privy to) created a complicated legal and institutional entanglement that has never been fully resolved.

The Onyx Hand's acquittal of Archie through their own tribunal further damaged the Guild's relationship with both Archie and the vampiric power structure. The Guild viewed the acquittal as a direct challenge to their authority—a supernatural faction overruling Guild jurisdiction in matters of magical misconduct. This institutional grievance has colored the Guild's approach to the Raventree crisis, where vampiric, fey, and other supernatural powers are active players.

Waluigi thinks the Guild-Archie conflict is essentially two control freaks arguing about who gets to control the same chaotic situation, except one control freak uses fireballs and the other uses paperwork. Neither approach has produced stability. Both have produced FIRES, metaphorical and literal.

Role in the Raventree Crisis

The Guild's involvement in the Raventree Manor situation has been both helpful and troubling. Their expertise in planar mechanics has provided critical theoretical frameworks for understanding the Planar Fracture—what happened, why, and potentially how to fix it. Without Guild research, the scattered fragments of Disaster Inc. would have even less understanding of the dimensions they're trapped in.

But the Guild is also STUDYING the fracture. Actively. With instruments and researchers and the kind of academic enthusiasm that prioritizes understanding over urgency. People are trapped in hostile dimensions—Waluigi was in the FEYWILD dealing with fairy riddles while the Guild was presumably writing research papers about the Feywild's fascinating planar mechanics. The disconnect between 'people are suffering' and 'what an interesting phenomenon' is the Guild's fundamental moral failure, and Waluigi doubts they'll ever recognize it because recognizing it would require them to view people as something other than data points.

Agent L

Agent L deserves separate mention because Agent L is better than the institution they serve. Practical where the Guild is theoretical. Engaged where the Guild is detached. Willing to get their hands dirty in ways that Guild policy neither explicitly authorizes nor explicitly forbids, which gives Agent L the operational flexibility to actually HELP people rather than just study their problems.

Waluigi suspects Agent L has internal conflicts about serving an institution whose priorities don't always align with doing the right thing. Waluigi recognizes this because Waluigi has spent his entire life associated with groups—Wario's Enterprise, various sports teams, the general category of 'villains'—whose priorities don't always align with his own. The difference between being PART of something and AGREEING with something is a distinction Waluigi understands intimately. WAH.

name: Peach Loyalists
title: The Ruthless Restorationists
motto: For the Crown, Whatever the Cost
summary: The Peach Loyalists are the faction that makes Waluigi most uncomfortable, and Waluigi has been uncomfortable in a LOT of situations. They fight for Princess Peach's memory and legacy, which SOUNDS noble until you see HOW they fight—with absolute ruthlessness, no quarter given, and a willingness to execute surrendering troops that would make the Iron Legion wince. Captain Toadette is the scariest person in the Mushroom Kingdom who isn't a dragon or a dimensional horror, and Waluigi says that as someone who has arm-wrestled Bowser.
description:
The Peach Loyalists exist because Princess Peach is dead and the circumstances of her death remain unresolved. That combination—grief and mystery—is DANGEROUS. It creates the kind of devotion that doesn't ask whether its methods are justified because the cause is too sacred to question. Waluigi has seen this pattern before on a smaller scale (sports fans who riot when their team loses) but never with this level of military capability and willingness to commit atrocities.

The faction is driven by two objectives: uncovering the truth behind Princess Peach's assassination and restoring her cause to dominance in the Mushroom Kingdom. Scouts like Embercap and Mistveil pursue intelligence leads with dedication that borders on obsession, investigating Peach's private chambers, past relationships, and the political networks that surrounded her. The information they've uncovered—including revelations from a gala event and secrets found in Peach's personal quarters—has deepened the mystery rather than resolving it.

Command Structure

The Loyalists operate with military precision under a clear chain of command:

**Captain Toadette** stands at the top—tactician, executioner, and symbol of the cause. She plans operations meticulously and executes them without mercy. Her reputation alone causes enemy garrisons to consider surrender, though surrendering TO Toadette is not advisable.

**Embercap** serves as Field Commander, leading assaults from the front. His crimson plume cuts through battlefield smoke like a wound, and his presence steadies wavering troops. At Bramblehaven, he was among the first over the walls, hammer cleaving through defenders as he gained the parapet.

**Mistveil** now governs Toad Town as Interim Governor, managing the provisional government while Toadette focuses on military campaigns. She was severely wounded during the Bramblehaven assault—struck by arcane frost and thrown from a ladder—but recovered under Dewdrop's care.

**Dewdrop** is Chief Medic, commanding the healers who work frantically behind the lines. At Bramblehaven, she shouted orders through thunder and cannon fire, dragging wounded soldiers to safety even as more fell frozen mid-climb.

**Big R** is the faction's heavy assault specialist—a living siege tower who goes first up every ladder and throws captured tanks through castle gates.

Captain Toadette
